construction: 63 parts in 8 evenly sized steps (6–12 placements each). Step 2: the differential with 12-tooth bevels. Step 3 (back view): the input double bevel and a U-joint enter the differential in its open 7×5 frame. Step 5: cross blocks and axles form the hub frames and outgoing half-shafts on both sides. Step 7: the shock absorber child.
interfaces: The parent places it with matrix `-1 0 0 / 0 0.932 -0.363 / 0 -0.363 -0.932`: about 21° about X plus a half turn. The input U-joint takes the drive; the shock's top end anchors to the body.
lesson: A driven Technic rear axle: a differential in an open frame, U-joints and half-shafts. The parent's matrix sets its tilt.
parent_context: The rear axle of `42075 - vehicle.ldr`, tilted under the rear, with the shock leaning up to the body.
reuse_notes: Keep the differential frame, U-joint input and half-shafts together. Derive the tilt for the new chassis instead of copying the matrix: the tilt sets the input shaft angle. Replace the generated spring mesh with a real shock absorber part before reuse.
